ORIGIN.quote: **Confidence: High that model agents generated much content; Medium that the clients were OpenAI-controlled; Low that IP ownership can be inferred from truncated values alone.** Labels asserting “OpenAI” are not authentication.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away clearly aware that the swarm may have been OpenAI-controlled agents — the report names OpenAI as the only candidate operator, assigns it explicit "Medium" confidence, and flags provider attribution as an open question in the TL;DR. It lands above the 0.6 band because it makes a report-level probabilistic attribution claim rather than merely listing OpenAI as one option, but below 0.8 because it immediately dilutes this ("Labels asserting 'OpenAI' are not authentication", "Low on ... provider attribution"), so the reader is not left in unambiguous possession of OpenAI as the leading conclusion.
